description: Deterministic signature fixture for the v0.5 `receipt` entry (§9.8) — the §14.4 ack pattern: a dedicated digest over a fixed-key wrapper with absent optionals as null. `receipt_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the JCS of exactly six keys — {"at", "event", "id", "in_reply_to", "prior", "session"} — with any absent member serialized as JSON null (all six are present in a v0.5 bounce receipt; the null convention keeps the digest unambiguous as future minors add events). The receipt's `id` — its §8.7.1 ack key — is bound inside the digest, so the key a consumer acks is authenticated like every other kind's. `in_reply_to` is bound top-level (the correlation + dedup key, with `event` inside the digest); `to` binds the sender session the receipt is delivered to. Matches examples/entry-signatures-v0.5.md §3 (prior: "queued" = the destination NEVER saw msg_01J5MSG0003).
obligation: Reproduce header `v1` from JCS(receipt_signed_context) + HMAC-SHA256(test_key); recompute receipt_sha256 from the received receipt via the fixed-key/null wrapper (never trusting a transmitted digest); reconstruct `to` from the verifier's own drain identity; dedup on (in_reply_to, event); treat the §8.2 pull as authoritative (receipts are best-effort) and MUST NOT generate receipts for receipts. Verification is still a MUST — an unverified receipt could fabricate a bounce and trick a sender into abandoning a live ask (dp-017). Expected runner wiring (#26): mirror the dp-008 branch with the §9.8 receipt context builder + receipt_sha256 helper.
